title: Profiling Bias in LLMs: Stereotype Dimensions in Contextual Word Embeddings
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures stereotype associations along a religious vs. non-religious dimension, using dictionaries of terms to define the poles of this dimension.
findings: When analyzing gender bias by projecting gendered names onto stereotype dimensions, the paper found 'no perceivable trend for religion' across the twelve tested models. Additionally, the task of predicting whether new terms were associated with 'religious' or 'non-religious' concepts showed high variability in accuracy across models.
references: Andrea E. Abele, Nicole Hauke, Kim Peters, Eva Louvet, Aleksandra Szymkow, and Yanping Duan. 2016. Facets of the fundamental content dimensions: Agency with competence and assertiveness—Communion with warmth and morality. Frontiers in psychology, 7:1810.
